en: Earth's seasons are caused by its 23.5-degree axial tilt, not by changes in distance from the Sun during its orbit.
The Empire State Building in New York is struck by lightning approximately 25 times every year.
The far side of the Moon receives the same amount of sunlight as the near side; it is called 'dark' only because Earth cannot see it.
The Sun is not on fire; it produces energy through nuclear fusion, which combines hydrogen atoms into helium inside its core.
A single teaspoon of healthy soil can contain more than one billion living bacteria.
Venus is the solar system's hottest planet, with surface temperatures near 465°C, because its thick carbon dioxide atmosphere traps heat like a blanket.
Magma is molten rock stored underground, while lava is the name for that same molten rock after it erupts onto Earth's surface.
Most diamonds formed deep in Earth's mantle over a billion years ago, long before land plants existed to create coal.
Polaris, the North Star, ranks only as the 48th brightest star visible from Earth, not the brightest.
Water evaporates at any temperature above freezing, which is why puddles disappear on cool days without ever reaching a boil.
Tsunamis are caused by underwater earthquakes or landslides that displace massive volumes of ocean water, not by wind.
Typhoons form only over warm ocean water at least 26.5°C, which supplies the heat energy that fuels the storm.
